# Who benefits

## Yves Hilpisch on coding {.pull}

> Programming is still the engine of quantitative finance, and GenAI only amplifies — not replaces — the need for precise, testable code ...

[[hilpisch.com](https://hilpisch.com/), summarizing [Why Coding Skills Still Matter in the Age of AI](https://hilpisch.com/why_coding.pdf), by The Python Quants with GPT-5, dated May 29, 2025]{.eyebrow}

## The same assistant, two users {.compare}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
[Expert]{.label}

- Asks for specific functions
- Recognizes when output needs changes
- Spots outdated formulas and assumptions
- Suspects a strong backtest
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
[Novice]{.label}

- Asks for a whole strategy
- Runs code without being able to judge it
- Asks the AI to fix errors it cannot diagnose
- Accepts a strong backtest
:::
::::

[Hilpisch (2025). His expert and novice cases are illustrative scenarios.]{.eyebrow}

## Four kinds of practitioner

| Type | Skills | Hilpisch's expectation |
|---|---|---|
| Super quants | Finance, Python, and AI tools | One may do the prototyping work of several junior analysts |
| Traditional quants | Finance and some coding, no AI tools | Effective, but slower |
| Non-coding domain experts | Finance only | Limited to tools others prepare |
| Non-domain tech experts | Technology only | Need finance partners to avoid misapplying AI |

[Hilpisch (2025), section 6]{.eyebrow}

## Reports from after December 2025

| Source | Report |
|---|---|
| Tal Fishman, Lord Abbett | "The error rate from a vague prompt used to be 70–80%. In December that flipped." |
| Ken Griffin, Citadel | Work done by finance PhDs over weeks or months is now done by agents in hours or days |
| Alejandro Lopez-Lira, Florida | AI systems are "at the level of a fourth-year Ph.D. student" |

[AI Street: [Fishman](https://www.ai-street.co/p/ai-turns-plain-english-into-backtests), March 3, 2026; [Griffin](https://www.ai-street.co/p/wall-streets-ai-push-hits-memory), May 21, 2026; [Lopez-Lira](https://www.ai-street.co/p/how-ai-runs-200-million-in-portfolios), July 28, 2026. Hilpisch's paper predates this period.]{.eyebrow}

## A randomized trial on learning

::: {.stats}
::: {.stat}
[50%]{.stat-value}
[quiz score with AI assistance]{.stat-label}
:::
::: {.stat}
[67%]{.stat-value}
[quiz score coding by hand]{.stat-label}
:::
::: {.stat}
[2 min]{.stat-value}
[faster with AI, not statistically significant]{.stat-label}
:::
:::

- 52 mostly junior engineers learning a new Python library. Debugging showed the largest gap.
- Those who asked for explanations or conceptual help scored higher than those who delegated.
- The assistant was a sidebar, not a coding agent. The quiz came right after the task.

::: {.footnote}
Shen and Tamkin (2026), [How AI assistance impacts the formation of coding skills](https://www.anthropic.com/news/AI-assistance-coding-skills), Anthropic.
:::

# Working with AI on Python

## What the agent does

::: {.steps}
1. Writes code and saves it to a file.
2. Runs it with a terminal command.
3. Reads the output.
4. Revises and repeats.
:::

Common uses in a quant project: boilerplate, explaining code or math, suggesting vectorization, and finding how a library works.

[Uses from Hilpisch (2025)]{.eyebrow}

## Arithmetic and code

- Levy changed the last digit of accounting figures, for example $7.334 billion to $7.335 billion.
- GPT-4's accuracy in predicting earnings changes fell from 60% to chance.
- Having the model write and run code for the arithmetic improved accuracy.

::: {.note}
Prompt: "Compute this in Python."
:::

[Bradford Levy, University of Chicago, "Caution Ahead," reported in [AI Street](https://www.ai-street.co/p/chatgpt-relies-on-memory-not-math-for-financial-predictions-study), January 12, 2025. The model is an older one.]{.eyebrow}

## Before it starts

::: {.prompt-box}
Plan how to do this before you start.
:::

::: {.prompt-box}
Tell me what you are about to do and what you are assuming.
:::

- Planning brings relevant knowledge into the conversation and creates steps you can check.
- Given an ambiguous request, it answers confidently instead of asking.

## How the model behaves {.compare}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
[Knowledge in use]{.label}

If it said last week that method A beats method B, but that is not in this conversation, it will probably use whichever appeared more in its training data.

Put the method you want in the conversation.
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
[Momentum]{.label}

After a roadblock it finds a way around, then another. It rarely asks whether a different path was better.

Restate the goal, not the obstacle.
:::
::::

## A project instructions file

```
# CLAUDE.md

Fundamentals: as-reported values, dated by filing date.
Universe: include delisted companies and delisting returns.
Time series: never shuffle. Train on the past, test on the future.
Returns: state costs and borrow assumptions in every backtest.
Numbers: compute in code. Set and log random seeds.
Runs: after each script, add the script, date, and output to RUNS.md.
```

Read at the start of every session in the folder. When you settle something, tell the AI to add it.

## Records for a research project

| File | Holds | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `CLAUDE.md` | What is always true | Read at the start of every session |
| `RUNS.md` | Script, date, and output of each run | Kept apart so it is not read every time |
| `memory/2026-11-05.md` | Decisions, rejected options, and the reasons | Each new session starts knowing nothing |
| Git | Every version of the code | The AI can run it and write the commit messages |
| Parquet files | Data | Fast, small, and left out of Git |

# Failures that raise no error

## Code that runs and is wrong

| Failure | What happens |
|---|---|
| Restated fundamentals | A 2009 portfolio uses numbers restated in 2011 |
| Fiscal period end instead of filing date | Weeks or months of free information |
| Only surviving companies | Every past portfolio holds firms known to survive |
| No delisting returns | A company that goes to zero is not recorded at zero |
| Shuffled cross-validation | The model trains on 2018 to predict 2006 |
| No costs or borrow | The short side is free |

## A question the schema cannot answer

::: {.prompt-box}
Count distinct tickers with data in 2005. Then count how many of those still have data in the most recent year, and show me some that do not.
:::

If the two counts match, the data contains only survivors.

## Independent checks

| AI-written code | Check against |
|---|---|
| Monte Carlo option pricer | Closed form, and convergence as paths increase |
| Greeks | Finite differences |
| Portfolio optimizer | Two-asset closed form |
| Data pipeline | A few rows by hand |
| Positive backtest result | Permutation test |

[First two from Hilpisch (2025)]{.eyebrow}

## Exercise: price a call

::: {.prompt-box}
Write Python that prices a European call by Monte Carlo under geometric Brownian motion: spot 100, strike 110, one year, rate 5%, volatility 20%. Report the standard error. Compare the price with Black-Scholes. Estimate delta by finite differences and compare it with the closed form.
:::

::: {.stats}
::: {.stat}
[6.04]{.stat-value}
[Black-Scholes price]{.stat-label}
:::
::: {.stat}
[0.45]{.stat-value}
[Black-Scholes delta]{.stat-label}
:::
:::

[Parameters from Hilpisch (2025)]{.eyebrow}

## Testing more ideas

- Fishman: projects that took weeks can be attempted in days or hours, so the firm attempts more of them.
- WorldQuant's student competition: more than 150,000 individual registrants in 2026, about double 2025.
- Exercise: have a model generate a few hundred candidate alphas, evaluate them, then apply a multiple-testing correction.

[AI Street: [Fishman](https://www.ai-street.co/p/ai-turns-plain-english-into-backtests), March 3, 2026; [WorldQuant](https://www.ai-street.co/p/more-brokers-let-ai-agents-place), August 27, 2026]{.eyebrow}

# From scripts to systems

## Keep what worked

::: {.prompt-box}
Create a skill for this, and save the code as a script that the skill uses.
:::

- The next run uses tested code. The model does not write it again.
- Pisaneschi, CFA Institute: when the model makes a mistake, add the "gotcha" to the skill file.
- Test the skill on a case you can verify before relying on it elsewhere.

[Brian Pisaneschi in [AI Street](https://www.ai-street.co/p/what-works-in-ai-and-investing), April 7, 2026]{.eyebrow}

## Split the work, then check it

- Lopez-Lira's portfolios separate macro analysis, company research, portfolio construction, and verification.
- Splitting keeps each context small. A full context degrades performance.
- A new agent checks the work: within the same session, "the model is biased by what has already been written."
- Agents are defined in Markdown files. An instruction added once applies to all future runs.

[Alejandro Lopez-Lira in [AI Street](https://www.ai-street.co/p/how-ai-runs-200-million-in-portfolios), July 28, 2026]{.eyebrow}

## Where the LLM sits

::: {.steps}
1. The model turns text into a number. Conventional code decides what it means.
2. The expensive model step is shared. Firms differ on the cheap steps after it.
3. Signals are formed without access to outcomes, enforced by what the code imports.
4. A positive R-squared is a hypothesis until it survives a permutation test.
:::

::: {.note}
High-risk finance processes suit workflows with checks at each step, not open-ended agents (Pisaneschi).
:::

# Teaching

## Hilpisch's recommendation {.pull}

> A student should graduate knowing how to code and how to use AI to help code, knowing the strengths and pitfalls of each.

[Hilpisch (2025). His related story, [The Maestro and the Apprentice](https://hilpisch.com/maestro_and_apprentice.pdf), asks how an unprepared manager directs powerful tools.]{.eyebrow}

## Questions for quant programs

::: {.steps}
1. Is Python a prerequisite, or something students learn while using AI?
2. Which code must students write without AI, and when?
3. Should exams test reading and debugging code more than writing it?
4. How do students reach the expert column if AI does the novice work?
5. What should a quant thesis disclose about AI use?
:::
